PR #70 is open: https://github.com/FChecklist/claude-control/pull/70

**Final checkpoint:**

- **Real gap count**: 105 itemized requirements from VERIDIAN_Architecture_v2.0.docx checked against real system state — **85 not_implemented**, **20 partially_implemented** (via real but narrowly/differently-scoped prior art: `prompt_gateway`, `knowledge_engine`, compliance-tracker's `litert-spike`/`llm-client.ts`/`permission-service.ts`, and the 20-Engines/10-Gateways architectural pattern), **0 already_implemented**.
- **Headline finding**: the document specifies a browser-first local-LLM "Prompt Intelligence Platform" (WebLLM/WebGPU/WebNN/DSPy/74 engines/41-stage pipeline/L0-L9 cache) that is fundamentally different software from anything currently built in claude-control, compliance-tracker, or this ops system's own prompt tooling — 9 tempting name collisions with the existing engine catalog were checked and explicitly rejected rather than assumed.
- **Real phase count**: 10 phases in the new plan, sequenced by real dependency (registry/schema foundation → compiler pipeline → governance → security → browser execution → caching → telemetry → DSPy/learning → gateway integration → YCML documentation), matching `auto_phase_continuation.py`'s exact schema and confirmed picked up by a real dry-run.
- Filed an explicit Owner decision (`veridian-architecture-v2-target-repo-anchor`) since this is the largest net-new engineering surface proposed this session and claude-control itself can't host any of it — flagged rather than silently defaulted, though phase_1/phase_3 (schema/governance design) don't block on it.
